  "summary": {
    "one_paragraph": "The governance record examines a proposed conversion of St Elsewhere's 6-bed Statewide Child Unit to a Hospital in the Home model for children aged 12 and under across a statewide catchment including regional and remote geographies. The signal distribution is 0 PROCEED / 11 CAUTION / 2 HALT. No Director endorses the conversion as currently scoped. The two HALT signals (Systems & Dynamics; Safety, Quality & Harm) characterise the current prerequisites as ungovernable within a clinically acceptable timeframe. The eleven CAUTION signals are conditional rather than permissive: each Director specifies what would need to be demonstrated before the risk landscape changes. The record is analytically coherent across all thirteen domains and operationally ungrounded at the same load-bearing points: the involuntary treatment legal pathway under the applicable state Mental Health Act is unconfirmed (named by eight Directors); the second statewide service fallback is unverified (named by eleven Directors); regional and remote delivery infrastructure is undemonstrated; family carer burden monitoring is absent; and the baseline outcome data needed for any evaluation is unconfirmed as extractable. The Adversarial Probe verdict is SIGNIFICANT GAPS, identifying that the status quo's harm profile has not been characterised with the same rigour applied to the proposed model's risks, and that the feasibility of the CAUTION prerequisites within any governance-acceptable timeframe has not been examined. The Stress Test assigns a fragility score of 9/10. The record is more analytically complete on why full conversion is premature than on whether responsible intermediate postures are operationally available.",
    "dominant_frame": "Conditional safety hold: the dominant signal across the record is that the proposed model's core safety prerequisites — involuntary treatment legal pathway, second statewide service fallback, regional and remote infrastructure, family carer burden architecture, and baseline data — are unconfirmed, and the CAUTION cluster is a conditional hold rather than a permissive signal. The equity aspiration animating the proposal is characterised as legitimate and the status quo's access harms as real, but neither the CAUTION nor the HALT cluster treats equity aspiration as sufficient to displace the unconfirmed safety prerequisites. The Adversarial Probe identifies a structural asymmetry in how the record applies analytical rigour: the proposed model's risks are characterised with precision; the current model's harms are not measured with equivalent specificity.",
    "decision_signal_interpretation": "Authoritative signal tally as supplied: 0 PROCEED / 11 CAUTION / 2 HALT. The two HALT Directors (Systems & Dynamics; Safety, Quality & Harm) are distinguished from the eleven CAUTION Directors by a threshold characterisation of governability, not by a different view of the underlying risks — the HALT Directors assess one or more prerequisites as requiring structural change on timelines outside the organisation's administrative control. The eleven CAUTION Directors each specify conditions that would need to be demonstrated before the landscape changes; none characterises the CAUTION signal as permissive. The signal distribution does not function as a vote and is not converted here into an institutional disposition. The Adversarial Probe verdict is SIGNIFICANT GAPS, identifying that the record has not examined whether the CAUTION prerequisites are achievable within a governance-acceptable timeframe and has not measured the current model's harm profile with equivalent analytical rigour to the proposed model's risks. The temporal dimension of the CAUTION signal — whether the named prerequisites are resolvable within months or years, and whether they have sequential dependencies — is unspecified in the record."

  "chair_resolution": {
    "decision_brief_status": "Complete — the governance record contains an unresolved tension between the CAUTION signal's conditional posture and the unexamined question of whether the named prerequisites are achievable within a timeframe that preserves the improvement opportunity the proposal represents, while the current model's harm profile remains uncharacterised alongside the proposed model's risks. The Decision Brief does not resolve this tension and does not select a pathway, rank options, or prescribe an institutional next act. The two HALT Directors and the eleven CAUTION Directors share the same view of the underlying risks but differ on whether those risks are governable within a clinically acceptable timeframe — a threshold disagreement that the governance record has not resolved.",
    "conditions": [
      "Governance authority confirmation: whether St Elsewhere holds delegated authority to make this reconfiguration — or requires ministerial or departmental approval — is unconfirmed. This is characterised upstream as a threshold question preceding all other governance acts. The condition remains unresolved.",
      "Involuntary treatment legal pathway: the legal and operational viability of involuntary assessment, treatment, and detention in a dispersed home setting under the applicable state Mental Health Act has not been confirmed by formal legal opinion. The condition requires legislative, regulatory, or formal legal clarification outside the organisation's administrative control. The record has not examined whether a model architecture explicitly excluding presentations requiring involuntary treatment would address this as a design parameter. The condition remains unresolved.",
      "Second statewide service formal agreement: the second statewide service has not confirmed capacity, intake criteria, or willingness to function as the escalation fallback, and no formal interoperability agreement exists. The record has not determined whether the gap is resolvable through agreement or is structurally precluded by the second service's mandate, catchment definition, or funding model. The condition remains unresolved.",
      "Regional and remote connectivity and escalation verification: digital connectivity, specialist workforce reach, and physical escalation pathways for regional and remote settings have not been verified at the individual address level against pre-specified minimum clinical standards. The model's equity claim depends on infrastructure whose adequacy is the central unverified assumption. The condition remains unresolved.",
      "Prospective baseline data establishment: whether the current inpatient unit holds structured, extractable outcome data usable as a pre/post comparison baseline is unconfirmed. If no usable baseline exists, evaluation collapse is characterised as a confirmed baseline condition rather than a contingent risk. The condition remains unresolved.",
      "Family carer burden monitoring architecture: no monitoring mechanism for family carer burden accumulation has been described in the proposal or confirmed as existing. Family carers are identified as the model's primary safety net and the least monitored element of the system. The condition remains unresolved."
    ],
    "irreducible_uncertainties": [
      "Whether the involuntary treatment legal gap is a design parameter resolvable by model architecture, a gap addressable through regulatory amendment, or a structural prohibition requiring legislative change. Formal legal opinion has not been obtained. The governance record characterises the gap as unresolved, not as a confirmed prohibition.",
      "Whether the second statewide service is structurally positioned to perform the fallback role regardless of willingness — specifically whether its mandate, catchment definition, and funding model permit this role. This requires different governance responses from a gap that is merely an operational confirmation problem.",
      "Whether the current inpatient model's harm profile — access failures for non-presenting regional and remote families, carer burden for co-residing families — is larger or smaller than the proposed model's risk profile. The comparative harm assessment is asymmetric in the governance record: one side has been characterised with rigour; the other has not been measured.",
      "Whether the CAUTION prerequisites are achievable within a timeframe that preserves the improvement opportunity the proposal represents.       "Whether responsible intermediate postures — specifically a modified model retaining inpatient capacity for involuntary presentations or a formally staged pilot with binding stop rules — are operationally available. No Director has examined what either would specifically require in operational, legal, and workforce terms.",
      "Whether the specialist workforce constraint is a two-year planning problem or a five-to-ten-year structural development challenge. No Director has confirmed headcount, geographic distribution, outreach capacity, or development pipeline data.",
      "Whether the current unit holds structured, extractable baseline outcome data. Absence of confirmed presence is not confirmed absence; the epistemic state is unresolved."

    "kill_switches": [
      "Any single instance in which a child enrolled in HITH in a regional or remote location experiences acute psychiatric deterioration and the documented escalation pathway cannot be activated within the pre-agreed response time — specifically, if transfer to inpatient care cannot be initiated within the timeframe specified in the escalation protocol — triggers mandatory immediate review of HITH enrolment eligibility for all non-metropolitan children and suspension of new regional and remote enrolments pending review. (Source: Safety, Quality & Harm)",
      "If legal advice confirms that no mechanism exists under the applicable state Mental Health Act to lawfully detain or involuntarily treat a child in a private home, the HITH model as proposed cannot be implemented for any child whose presentation carries a foreseeable risk of requiring involuntary intervention. This threshold is binary: either legal authority is confirmed in writing before enrolment commences, or children for whom involuntary treatment is a credible clinical possibility are ineligible for enrolment. (Source: Safety, Quality & Harm)",
      "If any enrolled child's primary carer reports being unable to safely manage the child's presentation, or if a clinician assesses carer capacity as insufficient during scheduled or unscheduled contact, and no alternative carer or clinical response can be mobilised within the timeframe specified in the safety plan, this constitutes a same-day escalation trigger. If this event occurs more than once in any rolling 90-day period across the HITH caseload, a mandatory service-level safety review is triggered. (Source: Safety, Quality & Harm)",
      "Any emergency department presentation by a currently HITH-enrolled child for a mental health reason triggers immediate case review. A rate exceeding two ED presentations per quarter across the HITH caseload triggers mandatory governance review of the escalation pathway model. (Source: Behaviour & Implementation)",
      "If the mean complexity score of HITH-enrolled presentations falls more than one standard deviation below the baseline established at model launch within the first six months, this triggers a mandatory audit of triage and acceptance decision-making, including review of informal scope compression in referral pathways. (Source: Behaviour & Implementation)",
